summary: The root ذرر primarily refers to scattering or dispersing small particles, like dust or grain.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: َرَّ, (T, S, M, A, &c.,) aor. َرُرَ, (S, M, Msb,) inf. n. َرٌّ, (S, M, K, &c.,) He sprinkled, or scattered, salt (T, * S, A, Msb, K) upon flesh-meat, and pepper upon a mess of crumbled bread with broth, (A,) and a medicament (S, A) into the eye, (A,) and grain (S, A, K) upon the ground, (A,) &c.; (T, Msb, K;) as also, inf. n. َرْ َرَةٌ: (K:) he took a thing with the ends of his fingers and sprinkled it upon a thing. (M.) You say, َرَّ عَيْنَهُ, (TA,) and َرَّ عَيْنَهُ بِال َّرُورِ, aor.

َارَّتْ, (aor. تُ َارُّ, S,) inf. n. مُ َارَّةٌ and ِرَارٌ, She (a camel) became evil in her disposition. (Fr, S, K.) Hence the saying of Hoteiäh, satirizing Ez-Zibrikán, and praising the family of Shemmás Ibn-Láy, وَكُنْتَ كَ َاتِ البَوِّ َارَتْ بِأَنْفِهَا فَمِنْ َاكَ تَبْغِى بُعْدَهُ وَتُهَاجِرُهْ i. e.

َرٌّ The young ones [or grubs ] of ants: (M, A, Msb, K:) accord. to Th, (M, TA,) one hundred of them weigh one barley-corn: (M, K:) or, accord. to En-Neysábooree, [who perhaps held َرٌّ to signify ant's eggs, ] seventy of them weigh a gnat's wing, and seventy gnat's wings weigh one grain: (MF:) or the smallest of ants: (S:) or small red ants: (TA:) or it signifies, (TA,) or signifies also, (A,) the motes that are seen in a ray of the sun that enters through an aperture: (A, * TA:) as though…
َرُورٌ A thing sprinkled: (M:) a dry medicament, (T, TA,) such as is sprinkled in the eye, (T, A, K,) and upon a wound, or sore: (T, TA:) or a kind of إِثْمِد [q. v.]. [Har p. 86.) See also َرِيرَةٌ.
ُرَارَةٌ What falls about, (M, A, K,) of perfume, when one sprinkles it, (A,) or of َرُور, (K, TA,) or of what is sprinkled. (M, and so accord. to the CK.)

َرِيرَةٌ (S, A, Msb, K) and (S, Msb, K) A kind of perfume, (Msb, K,) the particles of the قَصَبُ الطِّيبِ [or calamus aromaticus, also called قَصَبُ ال َّرِيرَةِ, q. v., in art. قصب ], (T, M, A, Msb,) which is brought from India, (A, Msb,) and resembles the reeds of which arrows are made: (T, A, Msb:) its internodal portions are filled with a white substance like spiders' webs; and when powdered, it is a perfume, inclining to yellowness and whiteness: (Sgh, Msb:) or, as some say, it is a mixed…

َرِّىٌّ a rel. n. from َرٌّ, (T,) (tropical:) The diversified wavy marks, streaks, or grain, of a sword: (T, M, A, K:) likened to the track of young ants. (M, A.) It occurs in poetry, in which some read دُرِّىٌّ [q. v.]. (M.) And (assumed tropical:) A sword having much of such wavy marks, &c. (K.)

ُرِّيَّةٌ, (S, Msb, K,) the most chaste form, (Msb,) and ِرِّيَّةٌ, (Msb, K,) and َرِيَّةٌ, this last without a sheddeh to the ر (Msb,) [respecting the derivation of which see art. رأ,] (assumed tropical:) Children, or offspring, (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) as also, (Msb,) of a man, (S, K,) [and of genii: see art. رأ,] male or female: (IAth:) little ones, or young ones. (Mgh, Msb.) Also (tropical:) Progenitors, or ancestors. (Msb, MF.) Also (assumed tropical:) Women. (Mgh, K.) Used in a sing.
مِ َرَّةٌ An instrument with which grain is scattered. (K.)
مُ َارٌّ A she-camel evil in disposition. (Fr, S, K.) [See 3.]

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
